subject: Hosted API commit tiers & monthly ramp — proposed schedule and discounts
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skybound.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@skybound.ai, Lisa Ward <lisa.ward@skybound.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing / ramp — initial ask

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Skybound is preparing to launch a generative search feature in Q1 and we expect heavy token usage during ramp. Before we get procurement involved, wanted to surface the ask so we can align on a commit + discount structure that matches our launch profile. High level: 

- Goal: Hosted API (text generation + chat) for public product launch.
- Target peak usage: ~150k USD/month in billed tokens at steady state (post-ramp).
- Initial launch ramp: 3 months from pilot to full launch; seasonality: slower in Dec due to holiday, ramp heavier Jan–Mar.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Do you support step-up monthly commit schedules with tiered discounts (e.g., Month 1 partial commit, Month 3 full commit)?
2) What per-token list price and discount bands look like at $50k/mo and $150k/mo commit levels?
3) Any clauses for true-up, seasonality, or minimums we should know about?

Procurement (copied) will need a sample invoice cadence and T&C. Can you put together a written proposal and a sample monthly commit schedule?

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Product, Skybound AI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skybound.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2025 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing / ramp — initial ask

Alex — thanks for the clear brief. Short answer: yes, we do step-up monthly commits and we typically model discounts by committed monthly spend rather than raw token counts. Below is a proposal to get the conversation moving; happy to iterate.

Summary proposal (Hosted API, per-token basis):
- List per-token (baseline) price: $0.00060 / input token, $0.00120 / output token (reflects current published rates).
- Commit tiers (monthly committed spend):
  • Bronze: $50k / month -> 15% off list per-token pricing
  • Silver: $100k / month -> 22% off list
  • Gold: $150k+ / month -> 30% off list
- Step-up ramp options: we support staged commits. Example ramp (customizable): Month 1 = 25% of target commit, Month 2 = 50%, Month 3 = 100%.
- True-up and seasonality: we include a 60-day rolling true-up window (monthly invoices, quarterly reconciliation). We can add an annual seasonality carve-out if you want a lower floor during known slow months (e.g., Dec).
- Quote expiration: 30 days.

Sample numbers for your stated target (target full commit $150k/month):
- Month 1: commit = $37.5k (25%); effective per-token = list * (1 - 30%) pro-rated to commitment band
- Month 2: commit = $75k (50%) -> moves to Silver discount band
- Month 3+: commit = $150k (100%) -> Gold band (30%)

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm desired ramp cadence (25/50/100 or something slower).
2) I’ll issue a formal quote + sample invoice schedule and DocuSign package for signature.
3) Connor (cc’d) will scope billing and invoicing cadence; Rishi will confirm approvals for the non-standard ramp.

I attached a sample invoice template and our commit terms for review. Quote valid for 30 days.

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0193
Attachments: Skybound_Invoice_Sample.pdf; Commit_Terms_Skybound_v1.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2025 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing / ramp — initial ask (internal)

Quick internal note — Marissa: the proposed 25/50/100 ramp is fine from a product standpoint but flags for finance: 
- Need clear true-up mechanics (we should state "monthly invoice, quarterly reconciliation with final annual true-up") and define what happens if Skybound underutilizes commitment after 6 months (refund? credit?).
- Recommend we include a 60-day ramp tolerance and a min-usage floor equal to 60% of each month’s commit for the first 3 months; if below floor, billable credit applies (not cash refund) — keeps financial exposure limited.
- For enterprise deals where they want a slower ramp due to seasonality, we can offer a graduated commit schedule but require a minimum guaranteed aggregate for Q1.

If you want, I can approve giving them up to 30% off at $150k commit but only if we add the floor + true-up language. Otherwise keep 25% as max for now.

Rishi
VP, Revenue Operations
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skybound.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Ward <lisa.ward@skybound.ai>, procurement@skybound.ai
Date: Mon, 06 Oct 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing / ramp — initial ask

Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. A few follow-ups after reviewing internally:

- We like the tiering but would prefer a slightly slower step-up given holiday seasonality: proposed ramp for Skybound: Month 1 = 20% commit, Month 2 = 40%, Month 3 = 70%, Month 4 = 100%. Does Redwood do a 4-month step-up?
- Can you provide a sample invoice cadence (monthly amount due vs. true-up) and a one-page clause that clarifies how credits vs. refunds are handled? Procurement wants to know if credits are the sole remedy.
- We also need a 60–90 day activation window for dev credits to support peak engineering/testing before production usage.

If those are acceptable we can route to legal/procurement for DocuSign. Can you draft the alternative 4-month ramp option?

—Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@skybound.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, procurement@skybound.ai
Date: Thu, 09 Oct 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing / ramp — initial ask

Alex — appreciate the specificity. We can do the 4-month step-up you proposed with the following clarified terms (please review):

Final proposed commit & discount schedule (Skybound AI target = $150k/mo full commit):
- Month 1 (activation): 20% = $30,000 (applies Bronze discount 15% for that partial month pro-rated)
- Month 2: 40% = $60,000 (Silver equivalent pricing band applied pro-rata)
- Month 3: 70% = $105,000 (approaches Gold — we’ll pro-rate discounts as you cross band thresholds)
- Month 4+: 100% = $150,000 (Gold: 30% off list)

Billing & true-up: monthly invoices issued at committed amount. Usage is reconciled monthly; credits applied on the next invoice if underutilized. We allow a 60-day mitigation window for one-off seasonal dips; sustained underutilization beyond that will be handled via credit (no cash refunds) unless otherwise agreed as a bespoke term.

Dev credits: we’ll provide a one-time dev credit pool of $10k for pre-launch testing, valid for 90 days from activation.

Next steps:
1) I attached the sample invoice and the commit T&Cs (same files as earlier).
2) If you confirm these terms, I will generate a DocuSign packet (HubSpot/deal link included) and route for signature.
3) Connor will confirm billing schedule and set up the invoice template in our billing system.

Links: HubSpot deal - https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/74321
DocuSign (draft): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/EXAMPLE-DocuSign-Skybound-Commit

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0193
